# Camouflare 2.0.2

Camouflare 2.0.2 bounds GET navigation stages, preserves time for eligible fallback and result collection, decodes compressed direct HTTP responses safely, and distinguishes terminal Cloudflare blocks from solvable challenges.

## Fixes

- Browser GET DOM readiness and commit grace each wait at most 15 seconds within the original command deadline. Navigation reserves up to one second for collection, reduced proportionally for short or setup-delayed requests.
- An already-eligible `ajax=true` timeout fallback retains up to 15 seconds or half the remaining navigation budget. Direct HTTP workers use the shortened deadline rather than a new full timeout. Committed pages retain browser challenge handling under the original request deadline.
- Direct HTTP GET decodes gzip and deflate, including concatenated gzip members and up to four stacked encodings, before charset conversion. Wire and decoded-layer limits apply under the request deadline. Invalid or unsupported compression returns `RESPONSE_DECODE_ERROR`.
- Confirmed Cloudflare-style hard blocks return `TARGET_BLOCKED` with `retryable: false` without invoking the challenge solver. Ordinary upstream HTTP errors remain API successes with their target status in `solution.status`.
- Default text logs include existing structured fields as redacted compact JSON. Prometheus error labels derive from the error-code enum.

## Client and transport contract

No new request or configuration fields are introduced. Session, proxy, screenshot, redirect, and POST transport restrictions are unchanged. POST cookies-only still does not read the response body. Failures after a POST is sent remain `requestOutcomeUnknown: true` and `retryable: false`.

Consumers must use `errorCode`, `retryable`, and `requestOutcomeUnknown`, not only the outer HTTP status, when deciding retries. Treat an ordinary target `solution.status=503` as an upstream failure, not a Camouflare capacity outage. Media-specific JSON/XML `Accept` headers deliberately select direct HTTP only for supported stateless proxyless GETs; browser-required or proxied GETs must not send unsupported application headers or drop their required egress.

The accompanying Events backend changes are in its separate repository and must be deployed separately.

## Deployment

Deploy the published index digest, not a floating tag, and preserve the recorded 2.0.1 digest for rollback. Check authenticated readiness and representative JSON, blocked, upstream-error, and navigation-timeout requests after deployment. Published workflow, commit, index digest, and platform digests are recorded in `docs/releases.md` after successful publication.
